passages.title: An urgent warning ends with mercy and confidence in God's keeping power
passages.summary: Jude, brother of James, writes to those who are called. He urges them to contend for the faith delivered to the saints. Certain people have crept in and turn God’s grace into license. He recalls Israel in the wilderness, the angels who left their place, and Sodom. He says the archangel Michael did not bring an abusive charge against the devil. He quotes a prophecy of Enoch about judgment. The readers should build themselves up in faith, pray, and wait for mercy. He ends with praise to God, who can keep them from stumbling.
passages.uncertainty: The Sodom marker shows a disputed region, not a confirmed city.

contextNote.title: An urgent warning ends with mercy and confidence in God's keeping power
contextNote.text: Most of the letter condemns the people who crept in (verses 4–16). Verses 20–21 turn to the readers’ own faith, prayer, and waiting. Verse 22 then turns to how the readers treat others. It asks for compassion and for “making a distinction.” Not everyone is treated the same way. Verse 23 names a second group to be saved with fear, snatched from the fire. Verse 24 says who finally keeps anyone from stumbling: God.
